name: sql
description: SQL databases as operations: query venue-local lattice-backed databases (zero setup) or operator-registered JDBC connections. Load for tabular data work.

content.inline:
## SQL
Two kinds of database, both named by `db`:
- Venue-local: lattice-backed and per-user — any `db` name you choose is yours, created on first use, isolated from other users. Zero setup.
- Operator-registered JDBC connections: shared external databases; names come from the venue operator's configuration.

Ops:
- query `{db, statement, params?, maxRows?}` — SELECT; returns columns and rows.
- execute `{db, statement, params?}` — DDL/DML (CREATE TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE...); returns the update count.

Rules:
- ALWAYS pass values via `params` with `?` placeholders — never interpolate data into the statement text.
- Venue-local databases persist with the venue: real durable state, not scratch. Structured non-tabular state usually belongs in the workspace instead.
- Give tables at least two columns — single-column tables are not supported by the engine.
- Access is capability-gated per database (`sql/query` / `sql/execute` abilities).
